stem: A client stabilized on lithium begins taking an NSAID. Which effect should the nurse anticipate?

options.A: NSAIDs reliably lower lithium concentrations and eliminate toxicity risk.
options.B: NSAIDs can decrease renal lithium clearance, increase serum lithium concentrations, and require closer monitoring.
options.C: NSAIDs have no interaction with lithium because lithium is eliminated only by the liver.
options.D: The combination always causes severe hypoglycemia.

rationale: Current lithium labeling states that NSAIDs can decrease renal clearance of lithium and increase serum lithium concentrations. Serum concentrations and clinical status should therefore be monitored when an NSAID is added or discontinued.
educational_objective: Recognize the lithium-NSAID interaction and the need for closer lithium monitoring.
source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_locator: Sections 2.3 and 7.1, Table 4: NSAIDs decrease renal lithium clearance and increase lithium concentrations
source_claim_supported: NSAIDs can reduce renal lithium clearance and increase serum lithium concentrations, requiring monitoring.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12/PDF p.16
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — drug interactions and therapeutic monitoring
correction_summary: Removed a blanket 'avoid all NSAIDs' rule and used the label-supported interaction plus monitoring response.
